identity.title: On the Commonality of 10-30 AU Sized Axisymmetric Dust Structures in Protoplanetary Disks

paper_type_evidence.quote: We retrieve the surface brightness distributions using synthesized images and fitting visibilities with analytical functions.

question.value: Do the highest-resolution ALMA (sub)mm continuum observations of four disks show common 10-30 AU axisymmetric dust structures, and do they relate to CO snowlines?

evidence.quote: Here we investigate the commonality of 10-30 AU-sized dust structures in a modest sample of four protoplanetary disks with the highest spatial resolution (sub)mm continuum observations to date.
Data on TW Hya and DM Tau were acquired out as part of the ALMA cycle 2 project 2013.1.00198.S
those on HD 163296 were obtained in project 2013.1.01268.S (Salinas et al., in prep)
ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00015.SV, ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00198.S & ADS/JAO.ALMA #2013.1.01268.S

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: TW Hya 349 and 661 GHz; DM Tau 329 GHz; HD 163296 233 GHz; HL Tau 233 GHz

evidence.quote: The baselines are generally $\sim$700 k$\lambda$, except that those for HL Tau extend to $\sim$12,000 k$\lambda$.

method.value: CASA 4.2 ALMA scripts plus iterative phase and amplitude self-cal

evidence.quote: We performed iterative self-calibration on both the continuum emission phase and amplitude to reduce the atmospheric decoherence.

method.value: Deproject uv with inclination and PA and plot against deprojected baseline; check imaginary part is flat for axisymmetry

evidence.quote: as also suggested by the flat distribution of their imaginary visibility components as a function of deprojected $uv$-distance.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit radial brightness with Gaussians modulated by cosines

method.value: Hankel transform of I(theta) = central Gaussian + sum of cosine-modulated Gaussians fit to visibilities; number of Gaussians set by number of visibility peaks; optional inner cavity with R_cav and depletion delta for HD 163296 and DM Tau

evidence.quote: The number of Gaussians is decided by the number of distinctive peaks in the visibility profile
We assume the source intensity is flat inside the cavity since fine structures inside 20 AU are unresolved.

fitting.value: Levenberg-Marquardt chi2 minimization; initial rho_i at visibility peak centers

evidence.quote: We use the Levenberg-Marquardt $\chi^2$ minimization algorithm to search for the optimal value of free parameters.

validation.value: HL Tau fit with truncated uv range compared with CLEAN image of full baselines

evidence.quote: the three major gaps (13, 32 and 63 AU) are reproduced nicely by the model fitting approach using the $\rho\le 2000$ k$\lambda$ data

method.value: Deproject visibilities, CLEAN with uniform weighting, azimuthally average

evidence.quote: We then derive an azimuthally averaged $I(\theta)$ from the images.
Consistent results are found over larger scales

method.value: Overplot literature midplane CO snowline radii on brightness profiles

evidence.loc: 3.3 Correlation between CO snowlines and enhanced continuum emission
evidence.quote: Figure 3 presents the mid-plane CO snowline locations on top of the surface brightness distributions in the four disks.
All visibility data were calibrated in CASA (version 4.2) using scripts provided by the ALMA staff.
For HL Tau, its known major gaps at 13, 32 and 63 AU are well recovered.
HD 163296 has two depressed zones centered near 55 and 100 AU
DM Tau has a shallowly depressed emission zone around 70 AU
has a turning point in the slope around 25 AU, followed by a plateau

findings_qualitative.value: All four disks are approximately axisymmetric with 10-30 AU radial structures

evidence.quote: the continuum emission of the four disks is $\sim$axi-symmetric but rich in 10-30 AU-sized radial structures

claims.hypothesis: Small-scale axisymmetric dust structures are common in disks
claims.experiment: Visibility fitting and CLEAN profiles of four high-resolution disks

evidence.quote: These results suggest that small scale axi-symmetric dust structures are likely to be common

claims.hypothesis: Continuum enhancements relate to CO snowlines
claims.experiment: Overplot snowline radii on brightness profiles
claims.result: Enhanced emission just beyond snowlines in all four
claims.finding: Possible causal link between snowlines and dust growth/trapping

evidence.quote: all four systems show enhanced continuum emission from regions just beyond the CO condensation fronts

why_this_method.value: No physical model for mm-dust surface density, so empirical approach

evidence.quote: Due to these uncertainties, we employ an empirical approach to characterize spatial structures in the surface brightness distributions

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Tapered edge, sharp edge, and sharp cavity models fail to reproduce visibility features

evidence.quote: These discrepancies suggest that a sharp truncation alone cannot fit the data
our proposed solutions are consistent with the data but other disk structures may also be possible.

referee_caveats_inferred: Only four disks, so commonality is weakly supported
Snowline correlation is qualitative with two model-based snowline radii
